payload.lessonGoal: Explain how DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash reduces KV cache storage through architectural and precision optimizations.
payload.learnerAssumption: A curious student with basic knowledge of LLM inference and the concept of a key-value cache.
payload.centralQuestion: How does DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash overcome the memory bottleneck of long-context serving?

requiredClaims.statement: Large KV caches strain HBM and SSD capacity, constituting the primary bottleneck for long-context deployment.
The Causal Encoder-Decoder architecture halves prefill computation by projecting decoder KV from encoder states.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash reduces global KV cache footprint to 890 bytes per token, roughly 1/4 of its predecessor.

requiredMechanisms.statement: Decoder global KV is projected directly from the final encoder hidden states rather than being computed layer-wise.
CSA2 shares global KV and indexer keys across layers to eliminate redundant storage.

scenes.teachingGoal: Demonstrate the multi-layered approach to shrinking the KV cache for million-token contexts.
scenes.learnerShouldUnderstand: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash uses architectural sharing, sparse attention, and low-precision quantization to drastically reduce memory demands.
scenes.mentalModel: A pipeline where input data is progressively compressed through structural sharing, sparse selection, and bit-depth reduction.

beats.purpose: Establish the problem of KV cache dominance in long-context models.
beats.narrationDraft: In long-context AI, the key-value cache grows so large it bottlenecks memory bandwidth and storage capacity.
beats.intentionalPause: Short pause to visualize the memory pressure.

beats.purpose: Explain how CED reduces prefill computation and storage.
beats.narrationDraft: The Causal Encoder-Decoder architecture projects decoder KV states directly from the encoder, halving the prefill computation needed.
beats.intentionalPause: Pause to show the projection flow.

beats.narrationDraft: Compressed Sparse Attention 2 further shrinks the footprint by sharing global KV and indexer keys across multiple layers.

beats.purpose: Explain the role of low-precision quantization.
beats.narrationDraft: By quantizing the main cache to FP4 precision, the model nearly halves its storage footprint without losing accuracy.
beats.intentionalPause: Pause to show the bit-depth reduction.

beats.purpose: Explain how SWA Bounded Replay handles persistent storage.
beats.narrationDraft: SWA Bounded Replay reconstructs local states from just the last window, allowing the removal of SWA from SSDs.
beats.intentionalPause: Pause to show the reconstruction window.

beats.purpose: Summarize the total impact on the global KV footprint.
beats.narrationDraft: Together, these innovations reduce the global KV footprint to 890 bytes per token, a four-fold reduction over previous models.
beats.intentionalPause: Final pause to emphasize the 1/4 reduction.

misconceptions.claim: Sparse attention alone solves the memory bottleneck.
misconceptions.correction: Sparse attention reduces computation, but the persistent KV cache footprint remains a bottleneck for HBM and SSD capacity.

evidenceRefs.quote: large KV caches continue to strain HBM and SSD capacity and data-transfer bandwidth. Together, these compute, storage, and bandwidth demands constitute the primary bottleneck
Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED) architecture, in which decoder global KV is projected from the final encoder hidden states.
CED successfully reduces nearly half of the prefill computation while maintaining performance comparable to the baseline.
KV entries are not derived from their respective hidden states... Instead, they are projected directly from the hidden state of the (L/2)-th layer
Compressed Sparse Attention 2 (CSA2), which applies cross-layer reuse to global KV (including main KV and indexer K) and Top-K indices
Sharing global KV and indexer K reduces duplicated cache storage.
CSA2 and FP4 KV caching reduce global KV cache storage to approximately 1/4 of that of DeepSeek-V4-Flash
we use FP4 global KV caches during training with only marginal performance degradation.
Compared with the FP8 main KV cache in DeepSeek-V4, this format nearly halves the storage footprint
SWA Bounded Replay, which approximately reconstructs the required SWA KV states by replaying only the most recent nwin tokens.
SWA KV is no longer cached in the persistent KV cache... With SWA Bounded Replay, the persistent KV cache footprint is further reduced to approximately 1/8
reduce its global KV cache footprint (always in HBM) to 890 bytes per token, roughly 1/4 of the corresponding footprint of DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash requires only approximately 1/4 as much runtime KV cache storage and 1/8 as much persistent KV cache storage
